tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search the live job board: postings pulled directly from employers' own hiring systems, 30-day freshness cap. Send job titles, skills and places, never CV text; put the place in location, not in query. Returns slim job cards with the board's parsed pay (salaryMinAnnual/salaryMaxAnnual) and seniority

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Full detail for one job id (from search_jobs), with the complete description and when the board last read the employer's feed. A resumebooster.work/jobs?job=<id> link's id is this argument (and fetch's and apply_myself's). For several ids at once use get_jobs. A dead id answers with what the board k

tools.name: get_jobs
tools.description: Full detail for up to 10 job ids in one call: the shortlist form of get_job. Ids that closed, aged out or were never on this board come back in `unavailable` with the reason, so one dead id never costs the others. Set includeDescription=false for cards and freshness only.

tools.name: check_jobs_open
tools.description: Are these postings still on the board? Up to 50 ids a call with no key, 200 with one: re-verify a saved shortlist before acting on it. Returns open:{id:boolean} and the closed ids, read from the board's index (a closed posting is one the employer's feed stopped listing), not the employer's site at t

tools.description: Help the person apply to one posting themselves, on the employer's own site. tools.name: board_stats
tools.description: Board statistics from a five-minute cache: servable and tracked posting totals, the count of company job boards with open roles (boards, not employers), the category slugs search_jobs takes, and what this connector does not hand on. Answers with no key and is never counted.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "apply_myself" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.detail: Description of "employer_growth" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "agent-mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_job, check_jobs_open, apply_myself, search, fetch · Private data: apply_myself, employer_hiring_record · Public sink: search_jobs, apply_myself.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_job, check_jobs_open, apply_myself, search, fetch · Private data: apply_myself, employer_hiring_record · Public sink: search_jobs, apply_myself

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
